industry.why: Overweight, carried unchanged and better supported. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): two houses now name staples as the place to be, Jefferies' desk (17 Oct) favouring 'pricing-power defensives such as staples and utilities' as energy inflation seeps into core goods and Danske (18 Oct) calling them 'not a bad place to hide'; energy, utilities and staples led the week and European defensives beat cyclicals by 4.7 points over four weeks (37-breadth-and-defensives.md). Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: C now, D prior, so the market has started to pay. Not Double Overweight: the multiples that make staples defensive derate with a 5.10% ten-year, and a defensive destination four weeks into a rotation is a crowded one. The sector rows carry B on Beverages, Tobacco, Household products, Food retail and Food production. Moves to A if defensives lead for a second month with the industry's relative strength at B or better.

sector.why: Overweight, carried, with a China warning named. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44): staples are the rotation's destination, but AB InBev's Asia-Pacific volumes fell 11% on Chinese beer demand (Outset Global, 29 October), and China is the weak sector within staples. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: B now, D prior, the market has started to pay. Two live holdings, Carlsberg (3.98%, with China exposure, Sell-side Momentum D) and Fevertree (2.00%), judged in component 4. Counter-case: the China leg is a company-level read on one brewer. Holds B with the staples industry; moves to A with it if defensives lead for a second month and the China read does not spread.

geography.why: Double Underweight, carried. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44): the French ten-year premium reached a record 150 basis points, 'a lot for a core European country' (Pacific, 26 October), the 2027 deficit is seen at 5.4% of output (Goldman Sachs, 25 October), euro-exposed assets underperformed their global betas because of France (GOAL, 26 October), 2027's 300 billion of issuance makes this 'just the warmup' and the election in May or June 2027 is the earliest point anything changes; against it, Moody's affirmation removed a sovereign tail risk (DNB Carnegie, 26 October) and the French Hidden Champions newsletter sees institutional outflows from French small and mid caps as a contrarian set-up. Ten Pool names, TotalEnergies at rank 24 near the Bench cut with a global revenue base the row does not describe well. Counter-case: the affirmation and the contrarian set-up. To D on the premium under 120 basis points for a month; back to C under 100.
